sentences.text: Serendipaceratops is a genus of herbivorous ornithischian dinosaur from the early Cretaceous of Australia that may be an ankylosaur.
The preserved length of the holotype ulna is about sixteen centimetres, featuring a broken olecranon process at the rear top and a flattened shaft.
Only one fossil occurrence of Serendipaceratops has been recorded.
The specific name arthurcclarkei honors science fiction writer Arthur C. Clarke.
The genus Serendipaceratops was named by Rich and Vickers-Rich in 2003.
The first bone of Serendipaceratops, an ulna, was discovered in 1993 near Kilcunda on the south-east coast of Victoria, Australia.
Serendipaceratops belongs to the parent group Ceratopsia and is classified within the class Ornithischia, with the type species Serendipaceratops arthurcclarkei.

A 2010 study suggested the ulna was more similar to the ankylosaur Minmi than to basal ceratopsians and lacked ceratopsian synapomorphies, a finding supported by a study by Angolin et al. that found the ulna lacked ceratopsian synapomorphies and was more generally similar to the ankylosaur Minmi.
A 2021 study classified Serendipaceratops as an ankylosaur due to the robust proportions of its deformed ulna.

The holotype dates to the early Aptian stage, approximately 115 million years ago, while other estimates place Serendipaceratops living during the mid-Cretaceous, approximately 116 million years ago in the Aptian stage, in what is now Australia.
Serendipaceratops lived during the Aptian stage, from 121.4 to 119.57 million years ago.
A 2014 study argued the taxon is valid based on ulna proportions falling within ceratopsian morphospace.
